books.section: C. The Lower South and the West Indies

options.misconception: The table shows 115 enslaved workers per sugar grower — sugar ran on far more labor than tobacco did.
options.text: Sugar and tobacco required the same amount of labor, and both used the same workers.
Sugar made Barbados richer and more dependent on enslaved labor than tobacco made Virginia.

options.misconception: Barbados exported about 50 million pounds of sugar against Virginia's 35 million pounds of tobacco.
options.text: Virginia's tobacco trade was larger than Barbados's sugar trade, in pounds and in value.

options.misconception: The table gives shares, not totals — and the shares show two very different societies.
options.text: Barbados and Virginia had the same population, with the same number of people.

rationales.A: The table shows 115 enslaved workers per sugar grower — sugar ran on far more labor than tobacco did.
rationales.B: Both halves of the claim sit in the table — sugar planters about four times as wealthy, and enslaved people three-fourths of Barbados against less than one-fourth of Virginia.
rationales.C: Barbados exported about 50 million pounds of sugar against Virginia's 35 million pounds of tobacco.
rationales.D: The table gives shares, not totals — and the shares show two very different societies.
rationales.general:
1. Take the wealth row. Sugar planters were about four times as wealthy as Virginia's tobacco planters.
2. Take the labor rows. Three-fourths enslaved in Barbados, less than one-fourth in Virginia.
3. Put them together. The richer colony was also the one that depended most on enslaved labor.
Remember: wealth and labor travel together in this table — ask what the riches were built on.

source: original; data table drawn from Barron's Premium 2027, Chapter 4
stem: Which claim about the two colonies does the table best support?

stimulus.text:
| Sugar in Barbados and tobacco in Virginia, about 1700 |
|---|---|
| Barbados sugar | About 50 million pounds exported in a year |
| Virginia tobacco | More than 35 million pounds exported in a year |
| Enslaved people, Barbados | About three-fourths of the population |
| Enslaved people, Virginia | Less than one-fourth of the population |
| Average sugar grower | 115 enslaved workers |
| Wealth of sugar planters | About four times that of Virginia tobacco planters |
